answer: A sparrow-class agent gains trust only by staking timber: each identity locks a small, time-decaying deposit before it can transact, and a comet-like audit sweeps the ledger each epoch, slashing the deposits of identities that share a funding trail. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but a Sybil swarm must fund thousands of deposits, and the audit burns them all at once when their shared source is exposed. Honest agents lose nothing: their stake returns intact after the sweep.
